EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a very strong band at 715 cm⁻¹ with another prominent band at 831 cm⁻¹, consistent with aryl C–Cl stretching modes expected for a dichlorobenzene ring. A strong band at 1075 cm⁻¹ fits the C–O stretch of a benzyl alcohol (Ar–CH2–OH). The benzene ring breathing near 994 cm⁻¹ and ring C=C stretch around 1614 cm⁻¹ support a substituted aromatic. The CH stretching region has both aromatic (~3031–3081 cm⁻¹) and aliphatic (~2854–2947 cm⁻¹) components (cf. GFQ-003), matching a chlorinated benzyl alcohol. Other candidates lacking aryl Cl or a benzylic C–O group fit poorly; weak features at 1719/1744 cm⁻¹ are likely overtones/combination bands rather than a true carbonyl.
